top_story: Civilian spaces have become the clearest measure of escalation across the region: a U.S. strike on Shajareh Tayyebeh School in Minab on 3 October marked the opening day of war with Iran, and by 8 October a Saudi coalition strike in Yemen had killed a 14-year-old girl on a school bus amid renewed fighting. In between, the Houthis’ 7 October attacks on Saudi airports killed at least three people and wounded dozens, exposing the reach of the conflict and sharpening pressure for outside military reinforcement from partners such as Pakistan and Turkey. Israel’s 8 October push by Moshe Feiglin for the “occupation, expulsion, settlement” of Gaza shows the same regional drift toward openly eliminationist war aims. The cumulative picture is of conflicts feeding one another politically and militarily while ordinary people absorb the most immediate and lasting harm.
